findings.proposedIrEvidence: The IR models clause (f) (board fees/optionholder payments), clause (l) (run-rate cost savings net of realized benefits), and the SUM covering clauses (m)-(r) (extraordinary items, independent-director payments, software costs, discontinued-ops loss, earn-out adjustments, Transaction Expenses) as unconditional additive METRIC_REFERENCE/SUM nodes, with no cap, gating condition, or UNSUPPORTED disclosure referencing the aggregate 15%-of-EBITDA ceiling on (f)+(l)+(m)+(n) addbacks.
findings.verifierReasoning: The source imposes an independently operative aggregate ceiling - amounts added back under clauses (f), (l), (m) and (n) collectively cannot exceed 15% of Consolidated Maintenance EBITDA (computed before such addbacks) in any Test Period. This is a real, quantitatively significant limitation on how much EBITDA can be inflated by these specific addback categories. The proposed IR includes no node, condition, or even an honest UNSUPPORTED placeholder representing this cap anywhere in the calculationExpression tree, despite otherwise using UNSUPPORTED nodes elsewhere in the same definition to flag unrepresentable mechanics. A reviewer relying on this IR could conclude these addbacks are uncapped, materially overstating EBITDA and any covenant capacity computed from it (e.g., leverage-based baskets).

findings.proposedIrEvidence: The clause (l) node is modeled only as SUBTRACT(SUM(restructuring run-rate savings, Permitted-Acquisition run-rate savings), actual benefits realized during the period), with no representation of the (x) 'reasonably identifiable and factually supportable' qualifier or the (y) 15%-of-Acquired-EBITDA sub-cap that applies specifically to Permitted-Acquisition-related synergies when combined with Section 1.07(3) addbacks. 'Acquired EBITDA' is listed in dependsOnTerms but is never actually referenced or used inside the calculationExpression.
findings.verifierReasoning: The source ties run-rate synergy addbacks for acquisitions to a specific quantitative sub-limit (15% of Acquired EBITDA, combined with Section 1.07(3) amounts) and a qualitative gating condition. Omitting this cap means the IR's clause (l) computation could allow unlimited acquisition-related synergy addbacks, which would materially change the computed Consolidated Maintenance EBITDA and any downstream capacity or compliance calculation that depends on it. The fact that 'Acquired EBITDA' is declared as a dependency but never operationally used in the formula is itself evidence that this cap was intended to be modeled but was dropped.
